text_source: TLG (Thesaurus Linguae Graecae, UC Irvine). NOT an independent transcription or OCR of Migne. The output is clean, fully-accented polytonic RUNNING TEXT (Word->Acrobat PDFMaker PDFs, not page scans, zero OCR noise) covering essentially the whole PG (161 vols) segmented by author and by individual CPG work/fragment-group exactly as TLG segments them (e.g. separate files 'Fragmenta ex libro ii contra Theodorum Mopsuestenum', 'Solutiones Vat 447'), with inline Migne column markers in TLG's volume.column format (e.g. '77.1072', '77.1073'). Full-text of the entire PG exists in only one electronic edition - TLG - so byte-clean accented coverage at this scale could not be hand-keyed; the empirical test (below) confirms it IS the TLG text.
license: Project self-claims '© 2006, University of the Aegean. Επιτρέπεται η ελεύθερη χρήση του υλικού με αναφορά στην πηγή προέλευσής του' (free reuse permitted with attribution). This grant is VOID for our purposes: the underlying bytes are TLG-copyrighted (UC Irvine), which the University of the Aegean has no right to relicense. Consistent with this, the official site was taken down 'για λόγους πνευματικών δικαιωμάτων' (copyright reasons) per istologio.org - the classic tell of an unauthorized TLG redistribution. Unlike DCO, the Aegean project shows NO TLG permission grant.
comparison_result: DECISIVE: byte-identical to TLG. Compared the project's 'De exitu animi.pdf' (ps.-Cyril of Alexandria, PG 77.1072-1089) against the known-TLG copy on Documenta Catholica Omnia (DCO file '0380-0444 - Cirillus Alexandrinus - De exitu animi - MGR.pdf', whose header states 'This text belongs to the Thesaurus Linguae Graecae (TLG), ... University of California, Irvine ... serial number 4090 119'). After normalizing each PDF's own page-header/footer banner and DCO's concordance markup, the Greek body is 29104 chars in BOTH and character-for-character identical: same words, same accents/breathings, same commas, same raised dots (·), same exclamation marks ('Οἴμοι! οἴμοι!'), same inline column markers '77.1072'/'77.1073' at identical textual positions. The ONLY divergences are DCO-side charset degradations (DCO renders μ as the µ micro-sign and strips the breathing on doubled-rho, 'ερ/αρ' where the Aegean copy correctly keeps 'ἐῤ/ἀῤ') plus DCO's added [00001]-style sentence numbers and appended Litterarum Conspectus index. In other words the Aegean text is the SAME TLG digitization as DCO - if anything a cleaner copy of the raw TLG bytes than DCO's. This is the identical pattern that disqualified DCO.
verdict: TLG-DERIVED DEAD END. Same disqualification as Documenta Catholica Omnia: the project redistributes TLG's copyrighted full-text of the Patrologia Graeca, not an independent digitization of public-domain Migne. The PD Migne content underneath is free, but THESE BYTES are TLG's, so the project is unusable for an open corpus (and its own 'free reuse' claim cannot cure that). Use it only as a navigation aid / proof that a work exists; for open text, OCR the PD Migne scans (the existing calfa-co 'pg' source) instead.
evidence: Project PDFs carry header 'Ερευνητικό έργο: ΔΡΟΜΟΙ ΤΗΣ ΠΙΣΤΗΣ – ΨΗΦΙΑΚΗ ΠΑΤΡΟΛΟΓΙΑ' and footer crediting University of the Aegean, Lab of Cultural Heritage Management (verified by downloading from the khazarzar mirror).

EMPIRICAL: Aegean 'De exitu animi.pdf' vs DCO/TLG 'De exitu animi MGR.pdf' -> Greek body byte-identical (29104 chars each; pdftotext + NFC normalization). Incipit in both: 'Φοβοῦμαι τὸν θάνατον, ὅτι πικρός μοί ἐστι. Φοβοῦμαι τὴν γέενναν, ὅτι ἀτελεύτητός ἐστι...' with identical punctuation including 'Οἴμοι! οἴμοι!' and inline markers 77.1072/77.1073.
DCO file header self-identifies its text as TLG, UC Irvine, 'serial number 4090 119', posted by 2008 permission of Director M. Pantelia - establishing the comparison baseline as genuinely TLG.

istologio.org (?p=1010): the University of the Aegean removed the digitized volumes 'για λόγους πνευματικών δικαιωμάτων' (copyright), after which they resurfaced on the khazarzar mirror - inexplicable for a true PD-Migne transcription, expected for unauthorized TLG redistribution.

Output characteristics inconsistent with OCR/independent transcription: flawless polytonic accentuation across hundreds of works (rare words like 'πρακτοψηφισταὶ' correct), work-level segmentation matching TLG/CPG (per-fragment files), and TLG-style inline column references - none of which a fresh OCR of Migne would produce.
Official site http://patrologia.ct.aegean.gr is dead (connection refused, 2026-06); only the khazarzar mirror keeps the files reachable.

Method note: the project distributes clean text PDFs (Acrobat PDFMaker 6.0 for Word), i.e. typeset from an existing digital full-text, not page-image scans - and the only digital full-text of the whole PG is TLG.
